svg.text: Inside each agent — the process every stage runs, and who acts at each step

amber = the Human’s step · indigo = the agent alone · purple = HAARPi, the conductor · green = a clean gate — solid = the work moves on · dashed grey = the step produces that artifact · dashed purple = the revision cycle
revisions
all comments resolved
1. rabbitHole surveys the literature
haarpi init: the Human sets the brief — the question, how many
sources, the Zotero collection
litrev.yaml
gather → searches, ranks and curates candidate sources, and writes
the collect-list for the Human to verify
ingest → fetches the references a reviewer NAMED,
matching what it can against Zotero and listing the
rest for `collect`
the collect-list
collect: the Human adds each real source to Zotero WITH its PDF —
verifying it exists, which is what guards against hallucinated citations
audit → re-judges the corpus for CONCEPTUAL
TRANSFER and moves the false-friends (shared
word, different sense) into a shared `quarantine`
collection — a move, never a delete
report → plans the review's sections and synthesises the FIRST draft
from the corpus, embedding it as it goes. Later, only a redirect
re-plans it
build → reads the audited Zotero collection into the
working corpus: candidates, citekeys, the ChromaDB
index, per-paper notes. `revise` reads that cache
and never embeds
the review .docx
revise → answers EVERY comment in kind: a tracked
rewrite where prose can carry it, a drafted section
spliced in at the comment that asked for it, the cycle's
corrections applied across the document
refs.bib
correct → replaces a term the reviewer says is
wrong across the brief, the litrev config, the draft
.md and the .docx. Deterministic, and applied
BEFORE the chain is built — so it queues no step at all
the embedded corpus
mindmap → places every cited source by how much of the review's
argument it carries, banded at the 5% / 25% / 50% marks of the
corpus
the contribution map
comment: the Human redlines the review — accept and resolve are
human-only
haarpi next → decomposes the markup ONE COMMENT AT A TIME
into what each asks for, then BUILDS the chain those needs require
litreview release
the released review
revisions
design agreed
2. rayleigh designs the study
rayleigh init: from the MINTED literature review and the brief,
Human + Claude co-design the research questions and the analytical
approach in a LIVE session — the strong-reasoning step, too
open-ended to default. It SPECIFIES only: building the code is
raster's job, downstream
designdocs/PLANNING.md
design_session → re-open the live session to address
the annotations and re-render the prereg. There is
no in-place reviser here: a decision cannot be
redlined, only remade — which is why ANY severity
costs the whole session
designdocs/EXPERIMENTS.md
designdocs/PRIORS.md
(prior ra* artifacts, indexed)
the framework schematic
(into the project figure pool)
renders the preregistration for review:
{cycle}_{short}_prereg_ra.docx, track-changes on
the prereg .docx
comment: the Human redlines the preregistration (accept and resolve
are human-only)
haarpi next → reads the markup. Clean MINTS the design and unlocks
raster; any unresolved comment re-opens the session
design release: the preregistration, committed BEFORE any code is
built
the minted preregistration
revisions
PASS · all modules green
digest accepted
PASS ·
next module
3. raster builds the code
raster plan: from the preregistration and the build brief, Human +
Claude author DESIGN.md and tasks.yaml in a LIVE session, and
FREEZE the test suite — written before the code that has to satisfy it
code/designdocs/DESIGN.md
raster plan → re-open the design session when the
comment is about WHAT was built: the modules, the
contracts, the tests
tasks.yaml
(modules, tasks, contracts)
raster freeze-review → the pre-queue gate: the cross-reference linter
over the frozen suite, plus an EXECUTED red-before-green. A suite
that passes before the code exists proves nothing
the frozen test suite
(unit tests, gates, goldens)
raster queue → flattens the module/task DAG into one ordered trundlr
chain: coding tasks to the GPU, gates to the CPU. A failure
auto-breaks everything downstream of it
raster build → re-run a task when the comment is
about HOW it was built. The frozen test still stands;
the code moves to it
raster build <task> → the LLM implements ONE task against its
frozen unit test, in a bounded repair loop that escalates worker →
strong. Green means commit and push; it cannot edit the test
the built code
(committed and pushed)
raster test <id> → NO model: the task's unit test, then the module gate.
Regression keeps the already-frozen tree green. A NO PASS does
not loop back — it breaks every task downstream
raster handoff → re-emit the digest when the comment
is about the WRITE-UP rather than the code
underneath it
the module graph
(into the project figure pool)
raster handoff → emits the Methods Digest for raconteur from
DESIGN.md + tasks.yaml + the frozen tests
the methods digest
comment: the Human redlines the methods digest (accept and resolve
are human-only)
haarpi next → reads the markup. Clean MINTS the methods digest;
any unresolved comment re-opens the build
build release: the methods digest, over a green frozen tree
the minted methods digest
revisions
findings accepted
4. rayleigh runs the experiments
rayleigh plan: the SECOND live session. Against the minted
framework and the code raster actually built — its entrypoint, config
surface, output format — Human + Claude author the EXECUTABLE
experiments: sweeps, cells, metrics, and a run_adapter bound to the
real code
results/designdocs/
experiments.yaml
rayleigh queue → linearizes the experiments into a trundlr chain, one
conduct node per experiment then a final process. The coarse chain
rides trundlr; each node still fans its cells out locally
cosmetic → `rayleigh process` re-reduces and
re-writes from the cells already on disk. NO new
data, so nothing is re-run: the analysis script and the
tidy table are durable, and the report is assembled
again around them
rayleigh conduct_exp <E> → expands the design into cells (one
parameter combo × one seed) and invokes the code's own entrypoint
per cell. It reimplements none of the model, skips cells whose output
exists, and stamps provenance
the cell outputs
(restartable, provenance-stamped)
rayleigh process_outputs → reduces the cells into a tidy table and
writes a base R + ggplot2 script that produces every figure, table,
statistic and regression. rayleigh does not compute the analysis: R
does, and the script stays runnable
extend → `rayleigh review`, an attended Human +
Claude session, because the comment needs cells,
seeds or experiments that do not exist yet. The
session decides which layer diverged and QUEUES
its own follow-on chain. rayleigh reports; it never
concludes
findings.json
+ the analysis script
the data figures
(into the project figure pool)
assembles the report around what R produced — the datestamped
write-up the gate reads
the results write-up
comment: the Human redlines the results write-up — accept and
resolve are human-only
haarpi next → reads the markup and sorts it by WHAT IT WOULD
TAKE: presentation only, or new data
experiments release: the findings, as preregistered
the minted findings
revisions
revisions
revisions
through-line agreed
structure agreed
manuscript accepted
5. raconteur writes the paper
raconteur onepager → the narrative through-line, in one page.
Everything below is built on it
the one-pager .docx
comment: the Human redlines the one-pager
narrative → `recut` the one-pager from scratch, with
the annotations as the brief. A through-line complaint
is always the one-pager's, however far down the
ladder it was raised — and the outline is never rebuilt
from a through-line the author has not signed off
haarpi next → cosmetic re-runs `onepager`; anything heavier IS a
narrative complaint, because a structure objection to a five-beat
narrative means the through-line is wrong — so it re-cuts
one-pager release
the minted one-pager
raconteur venue → a slate of candidate venues, analysed from the
narrative
the venue slate
the Human picks the venue — and with it the format, the length, and the
submission requirements everything downstream is sized to
raconteur skeleton → phase one: the sections and subsections, and the
words each can afford
the skeleton
(sections + word budget)
raconteur outline → phase two: the content beats, written onto the
APPROVED skeleton
cosmetic → answered in place, on the rung the
comment sits on: `draft` redlines the manuscript,
`outline` re-runs phase two, `skeleton` re-runs
phase one. The cheapest route, and the only one that
changes nothing above it
the outline .docx
comment: the Human redlines the outline (or asks to refine one
section)
haarpi next → cosmetic and structural both re-run `outline`; a
narrative objection goes back to the one-pager
outline release
the minted outline
raconteur draft → the full manuscript, written from the releases
upstream: the outline for structure, the litreview, methods digest and
findings for content
upstream_literature → escalates OUT of this stage:
gather, collect, report and comment, back in the
literature review. The claim the comment doubts is
not in the corpus yet
the manuscript .docx
comment: the Human redlines the manuscript — accept and resolve
are human-only
haarpi next → routes by what the comment costs: in place, re-outline,
re-cut, or back out to the literature
paper release: the manuscript
the minted manuscript
raconteur package → assembles and compiles the venue submission
the venue submission
(assembled + compiled)
revisions
deck accepted
6. razzle makes the presentation
razzle interview: a pure-python session — NO model — that captures
the facts a tool must never invent: which formats to build, and per
format the venue, date, presenting authors, affiliation logos and
funders. It writes the manifest and prints the per-format command. It
queues nothing, because the deck stage is tracked by its
DELIVERABLE
deck_formats + decks
(written to the manifest)
razzle deck --format <fmt>: gathers the manuscript, one-pager,
figures and claims, then hands over to an INTERACTIVE session that
authors the deck spec — the only model call in the stage. The
presenting byline is applied deterministically afterwards, because
who presents is a fact, not a guess
deck_session → re-open `razzle deck` to address the
PowerPoint comments, revise the spec and
re-render. Any severity, like every other attended
stage: the spec is a set of authoring decisions, and a
decision is remade rather than redlined
slides/{fmt}/spec.json
(the durable artifact)
python-pptx clones the master's layouts by ROLE and fills them: no
model, no GPU. A missing master degrades to writing the spec
rather than failing. Masters and logos live outside the repo, in
~/.config/haarpi/razzle/
razzle render → when the spec is right and only the
rendering is wrong, re-render from spec.json. No
model, no GPU, no cost — which is why the spec, not
the .pptx, is the durable artifact
the branded .pptx
comment: the Human redlines the .pptx IN PLACE with PowerPoint
comments — accept and resolve are human-only
haarpi next → mints the deck to its token-free name; any unresolved
comment re-opens the deck session
deck release — ONE PER CHOSEN FORMAT (short talk, long talk,
poster)
the minted deck,
one per format
the review unlocks the design
the prereg unlocks the build
the methods digest unlocks the experiments
the findings unlock the paper
the submission unlocks the deck
